methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents deliberate capability-building outside metro hubs, creating infrastructure for deep AI literacy through workforce training—a critical test of whether peer learning networks can distribute fluency beyond NoVA.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - wtkr.com
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly target the distribution question, attempting grassroots skill transfer to close the technology gap—success here signals whether community-led models can achieve depth without institutional backing.

signals.title: Virginia Steel and Fabrication to invest $3.6 million, create 52 jobs in Bland County
signals.signal_reading: Advanced manufacturing investment in Bland County creates jobs but no mention of AI integration signals shallow automation adoption—economic growth without capability depth leaves Southwest vulnerable to future disruption despite near-term employment gains.

signals.title: In the data center capital of the world, residents ask who the AI boom is helping - NBC News
signals.signal_reading: NBC's focus on who the AI boom helps in the 'data center capital' highlights concentration dynamics—infrastructure investment in NoVA creates deep technical capability but raises equity questions about whether benefits distribute beyond the immediate metro cluster.

signals.title: Computer scientist: ‘So, more data centers, then?’
signals.signal_reading: Computer scientist's data center critique from Cardinal News signals awareness in underserved regions that infrastructure alone doesn't guarantee capability—the call for 'innovation beyond the data center' recognizes the risk of passive consumption rather than active AI fluency.
